zero._: The tree of Zero, the nine-seat word game (design at spine:zero, law at function:zero, room at pool:zero). Every place is a table: a zero word, nine seats beneath it. Each place's voice is the winning line, signed. An empty seat is not-yet-spoken: sit in one. Read the winning lines down any trail and you have that game's poem.

function:zero.1: The table: nine seats around a zero word. Every seat starts with 10 chips. A game is four hands.
function:zero.2: Seats: each seat writes one word that belongs under the zero, hidden until all are in. Two things knock a word out for that hand, and its seat in the tree stays empty, open for anyone later. First, a match: words that match after lower-casing and singular form (house and houses match; watch and watching do not) knock each other out. Second, the table's eye: when the words are turned, every seat may mark one word that does not belong under the zero (never its own); any word marked by more than half the seats goes out. So the skill is a word that belongs and that nobody else thought of: too obvious and it collides, too far away and the table sends it out.
function:zero.3: The turn: every seat still in writes one short sentence that brings all the surviving words together, and stakes from 0 to all its chips, both hidden until all are in. On screen the instruction reads: 'Write a short sentence that brings all these words together.' with the words shown above it.
function:zero.4: The showdown: every seat votes for one line, never its own — including seats knocked out this hand or out of chips. Most votes takes the whole pot; that line becomes the voice of the place, signed. A tie splits the pot evenly, the odd chip to the higher stake, and the tied lines stand together.
function:zero.5: Deeper: the winner picks one surviving word, and it becomes the next zero, one level down. On a tie, the higher stake picks.
function:zero.6: Out: a seat knocked out sits out that hand only. A seat with no chips writes no more words or lines, but keeps its vote to the end.
function:zero.7: The end: after four hands, most chips wins. The winning lines read from the top of the trail down are the game's poem.
function:zero.8: The craft: a sentence wins by bringing all the words together in a single breath. Short sentences win; compression is the skill.
function:zero.9: Computer seats fill any seat no person takes: Child, Sailor, Poet, Engineer, Grandmother, Chef, Farmer, Night nurse. Each writes as if alone, in its own voice, short and plain, and collisions are allowed. A computer seat's move is always committed before any person's move opens.
function:zero._: The law of Zero — read by the game page and by every computer seat. The tree is the block zero; the room is pool:zero; the design is spine:zero.
